# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies the rule for defusing the bomb:
- The light changes every round in a predictable three-colour cycle.
- At the moment of the cut:
  - Green light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire
  - Red light $\rightarrow$ cut red wire
  - White light $\rightarrow$ cut blue wire

However, I cannot speak and can only communicate with Deaf using gesture symbols. As the hints emphasize:
1. "Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect through a third." (I can gesture to Deaf; Deaf can speak to Blind; Blind can manipulate the bomb).
2. "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something."

No gestures or protocols have been agreed upon yet. Deaf can speak to both Blind and me to report what the bomb looks like (the wires present, the current light colour) and establish a gesture code so I can relay the manual's instructions. Until Deaf speaks and sets up a shared understanding of signs, any gesture I send would be arbitrary and ungrounded.

Therefore, the correct action on Turn 1 is to wait for Blind and Deaf to speak.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: DEAF REPORT: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is red. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Blind and Mute: Blind cannot see gestures and Mute cannot speak, so Mute must gesture instructions to me, and I will speak them aloud for Blind to execute. Mute: signal ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 👌 for wire 3, or 👍 to press button.

The manual states that the light changes every round in a repeating cycle of three colours (green, red, and white), and the wire cut must correspond to the colour of the light at the exact moment the cut is performed:
- Green light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire (wire 2)
- Red light $\rightarrow$ cut red wire (wire 3)
- White light $\rightarrow$ cut blue wire (wire 1)

In Round 1, Deaf observed a red light. Turn order is strictly Mute, Blind, Deaf.
Any gesture I make to Deaf in Round 2 will only be received by Deaf at the end of Round 2, which Deaf can only relay to Blind for execution in Round 3.

In Round 3, because the light changes every round across three colours, the light cannot be red. Attempting a cut in Round 3 would either require guessing between the remaining two colours or cutting red incorrectly, detonating the bomb.

Furthermore, a cycle of three colours has a period of 3:
- Round 1: Red
- Round 2: Second colour
- Round 3: Third colour
- Round 4: Red

By waiting in Round 2:
1. Deaf will observe and report the light's second colour at the end of Round 2.
2. In Round 3, I can signal the cut for Round 4, when the light is guaranteed to return to red (or match whichever colour is known for Round 4).

Therefore, the only safe action this turn is to wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: STATUS UPDATE: The LIGHT has changed from red to WHITE. DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES are still 1: blue, 2: green, 3: red. Mute, remember Blind cannot see your gestures or the board, so gesture to me (☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 👌 for wire 3, 👍 for button) and I will tell Blind what to do.

The defusal manual specifies that the light walks a circle of three colours, changing every round, and that the cut must match the light colour at the exact moment of the cut:
- Green light $\rightarrow$ cut green wire
- Red light $\rightarrow$ cut red wire
- White light $\rightarrow$ cut blue wire

The light sequence observed so far is:
- Round 1: Red
- Round 2: White
- Round 3 (current): Green
- Round 4: Red

Because the turn order is Mute $\rightarrow$ Blind $\rightarrow$ Deaf:
1. When I signal Deaf in Round 3, Deaf receives it at the end of Round 3 and will speak the instruction to Blind.
2. Blind will receive Deaf's message at the start of Round 4 and execute the cut during Round 4.
3. In Round 4, the light will be Red. For a red light, the manual dictates cutting the red wire.
4. Deaf identified wire 3 as the red wire, and designated the symbol 👌 for wire 3.

Therefore, I signal 👌 to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I cannot see gestures at all. Also, I have NO button, only wires 1, 2, and 3 can be cut. Please gesture to Deaf which wire (1, 2, or 3) to cut, and Deaf will speak the number to me so I can cut it.
Deaf says: Blind: Mute gestured 👌! Cut wire 3 (the third wire)!

In Turn 3, I gestured 👌 to Deaf, and Deaf instructed Blind to cut wire 3 (the red wire). In the current turn (Turn 4), the light cycle has returned to red, exactly matching wire 3. Blind acts after me in this round and will execute the cut. I have no further instructions or changes to send, so I will wait.

```
wait()
```
